annotations.title: How later courts described this case

description: Given one opinion id, returns the one-line parentheticals later courts wrote about that case, verbatim. A parenthetical is the later court’s own characterisation: not a holding of the described case, not a summary written by this service, and not treatment, validity or "good law". Each item names the opinion that wrote it (case name, date, citation_count). Near-duplicates ship pre-grouped by CourtListener/FLP (group_id); one row per group is returned (highest score, ties by id; that pick is this service’s, and score has no documented meaning), and group_size counts the lines it stands for. Coverage is partial and skewed toward frequently cited opinions (6,561,861 parentheticals): an empty result means none was extracted for this opinion. At most 2000 are examined a request (examined_capped=true marks a floor); unattributable_in_window counts lines whose author is absent from the mirror. same_case_opinions and most_parentheticals_on name a sibling opinion carrying more (Miranda v. Arizona: 107252 has 1; lead opinion 9423233, 1,524). Case law in this mirror ends 2026-09-30 (exact scan of all 10,174,547 case records): a thin or empty result for recent authority means the collection ends there, not that no such case exists. Every response carries a "note" and a coverage_note. The sources tool returns this tool’s full coverage statement.

id.description: the DESCRIBED opinion id — the case you want later courts' descriptions of (from a search/fts/semantic/similar result opinion_id)

limit.description: max groups returned, 1-25 (default 10); one representative parenthetical per group
